scope.description: Named public-demand dossier for the Government of Canada's Defence Drone Initiative, combining the official release, a CanadaBuys marketplace trace, related official drone-innovation context, and independent secondary coverage.

source.title: Government of Canada launches Defence Drone Initiative to strengthen Canada's sovereign defence capabilities
source.locator: News release: initial capability areas, Request for Supply Arrangement, supplier qualification and timing
source.summary: National Defence announced the Defence Drone Initiative as a program and supplier marketplace intended to accelerate Canadian uncrewed and autonomous systems for the Canadian Armed Forces and Canadian Coast Guard.

leads.evidenceLocator: The release identifies the DDI, its six initial capability areas, the RFSA process, and its stated purpose of connecting operational needs with Canadian industrial capacity.
followUpQuestions: Should this marketplace and program remain a distinct public demand source alongside broader Defence Industrial Strategy demand records?
Which future CanadaBuys amendments, solicitations, awards, or supplier announcements should be added as refresh evidence?
reviewWarnings: Qualification under the RFSA does not itself create a contract, supplier endorsement, or procurement eligibility conclusion.
The published capability areas are a public program signal and may be amended as the marketplace evolves.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: Official National Defence release established the program, user communities, capability areas, supplier process, and public caveat on qualification.
CanadaBuys trace independently confirmed the W8703-270055 Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace tender title and public publication date.
Independent coverage corroborated the marketplace framing and was retained as secondary context only; canonical claims remain tied to government sources.

leads.title: Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace
candidateRequirements: Canada seeks a qualified supplier marketplace that can support testing, prototype development, limited acquisition, and potential production of uncrewed and autonomous systems for CAF and Canadian Coast Guard operational needs.

The public program identifies low-cost tactical ISR drones, ground logistics systems, uncrewed maritime surface and underwater systems, counter-drone interceptors, standardized drone munitions, and deep precision strike systems as initial capability areas.
